# Node catalog

<!-- Generated by `node dist-cli/thingstudio-compile.mjs --describe-all --markdown`. Do not edit by hand: a test fails when it is out of date. -->

This is the flow-file reference. It lists every node a `.flow.json` can use, with the exact names a flow file needs:
the node's type, its ports, and its properties with their types, defaults and allowed values. The editor's code
generates it, so it matches what the compiler accepts.

It does not explain how to use a node. Each entry links to the node's page, which says what the node does and what
each property means. To build a flow in the editor, start from the [node reference](nodes/index.md). To write or check
a flow file without the editor, see [Check a flow without the editor](check-a-flow.md) and [AI authoring](ai-authoring.md).

In a flow file a node's type is `thingstudio/` followed by the type shown here: `wifi_status` is written
`thingstudio/wifi_status`. A property's editor label is the name the node's page uses for it. A port described as
"message, payload bool" carries a message whose `payload` is a bool.

Ports are numbered from 0 in a flow file's `edges`: `[fromNodeId, outputNumber, toNodeId, inputNumber]`, in the order listed here.

| `property` | property / name | string | `"payload"` |  |
| `valueFrom` | value from | string | `"literal"` | one of `literal`, `msg`, `flow` |
| `valueType` | literal type | string | `"string"` | one of `string`, `number`, `bool` |

## hardware

### adc

Reads an ADC pin and sends a message when the reading leaves, or returns to, a set range.

Type: `adc`. Kind: source. Palette group: hardware.

Properties explained: [adc](nodes/adc.md)

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: message, any payload

| Property | Editor label | Type | Default | Allowed values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin` | pin | number | `34` | the ADC pin to read; on ESP32, use an ADC1 pin if the flow uses WiFi (ADC2 can't with the radio on) |
| `mode` | mode | string | `"relative"` | one of `relative`, `absolute`; relative (current value +- delta) or absolute (lower..upper) |
| `delta` | delta (counts) | number | `2000` | relative mode: how far the reading must move from the last sent one to fire |
| `lower` | lower | number | `0` | absolute mode: the low bound |
| `upper` | upper | number | `50000` | absolute mode: the high bound |
| `sense` | sense | string | `"outside"` | one of `outside`, `inside`; outside (fire when the value leaves the bounds) or inside (fire when it returns) |
| `pollMs` | poll (ms) | number | `0` | also send every this many ms; 0 = only on a bounds crossing |

### ble advertise

### ble scan

Listens for Bluetooth LE advertisements, such as beacons and BLE sensors, and sends one message per advertisement.

Type: `ble_scan`. Kind: source. Palette group: network.

Properties explained: [ble scan](nodes/ble-scan.md)

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: message, payload bytes
- Needs hardware: ble (checked against the board at compile time)

| Property | Editor label | Type | Default | Allowed values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `namePrefix` | name starts with | string | `""` | only devices whose advertised name starts with this; many send a name only to an active scan |
| `addr` | address | string | `""` | only this device, aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff |
| `mfrId` | manufacturer id | string | `""` | only this manufacturer id, decimal or hex with 0x (0x0499 Ruuvi) |
| `serviceUuid` | service UUID | string | `""` | only advertisements listing this service or carrying its data: 16-bit (fcd2, BTHome) or 128-bit |
| `active` | active scan | boolean | `false` | also request each device's scan response (usually its name) |
| `repeatMs` | repeat window (ms) | number | `1000` | drop an advertisement identical to the same device's last one within this time; 0 sends all |
| `scanIntervalMs` | scan interval (ms) | number | `320` | how often the radio listens, 2.5-10240 ms; every ble_scan in a flow must agree |
| `scanWindowMs` | scan window (ms) | number | `30` | how long each listen lasts, up to the interval; longer misses less and leaves WiFi less time |

## Config nodes

A config node is listed under `configs` in a flow file as `{id, type, properties}`, with the full type shown here. A node names it by id in a property such as `i2cConfigId`. Credentials are saved by name (`credentialName`), never as secrets in the file.

### BLE

Type: `thingstudio/config/ble` (one per flow).

- `name`, text: What other devices show when they find the board, up to 26 bytes. Shorter leaves more room in an advertisement.

Defaults: `{"name":"thingstudio"}`

### BLE peer

Type: `thingstudio/config/ble-peer`.

- `addr`, text: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff. Leave blank to find the device by its name instead.
- `namePrefix`, text: Used when there's no address. Phones change their address; most sensors don't.
- `timeoutMs`, number: How long finding and connecting may each take before it tries again.

Defaults: `{"addr":"","namePrefix":"","timeoutMs":10000}`

### GUI theme

Type: `thingstudio/config/gui-theme`.

- `preset`, select: one of `dark-slate`, `light-paper`, `vivid`, ``; Choosing a starting point replaces the colours below; editing one makes the theme custom.
- `bg`, colour
- `card`, colour
- `fg`, colour
- `muted`, colour
- `track`, colour
- `accent`, colour
- `on_accent`, colour
- `ok`, colour
- `warn`, colour
- `alarm`, colour

Defaults: `{"preset":"dark-slate","bg":4258,"card":8484,"fg":65535,"muted":35953,"track":16904,"accent":16113,"on_accent":2113,"ok":15974,"warn":64608,"alarm":63488}`

### I2C bus

Type: `thingstudio/config/i2c-bus`.

- `bus`, number
- `scl`, pin
- `sda`, pin
- `freq`, number: 100000 suits most sensors; 400000 for displays that can take it.

Defaults: `{"bus":0,"scl":null,"sda":null,"freq":100000}`

### MQTT Broker

Type: `thingstudio/config/mqtt-broker` (one per flow).

- `credentialName`, credential

Defaults: `{"credentialName":""}`

### Touch panel

Type: `thingstudio/config/touch-panel`.

- `controller`, select: one of `ft6336u`; Other controllers (GT911, CST820) aren't supported yet.
- `i2cConfigId`, configRef: the id of a `thingstudio/config/i2c-bus` config
- `address`, text: 7-bit, e.g. 0x38.
- `rstPin`, pin: Blank if the panel has none.
- `pollMs`, number
- `width`, number
- `height`, number: The panel's own size. If the display is rotated, tick swap/flip until a touch lands where you pressed.
- `swapXY`, boolean
- `flipX`, boolean
- `flipY`, boolean

Defaults: `{"controller":"ft6336u","i2cConfigId":"","address":"0x38","rstPin":"","pollMs":20,"width":320,"height":480,"swapXY":false,"flipX":false,"flipY":false}`

### web server

Type: `thingstudio/config/web-server`.

- `port`, number: The port the board's HTTP server listens on (80 is the ordinary one). Remote displays log in at http://<board>:<port>/ts/remote/.

Defaults: `{"port":80}`

### WiFi

Type: `thingstudio/config/wifi` (one per flow).

- `credentialName`, credential
- `security`, select: one of `password`, `open`, `unmanaged`
- `allowReprovisioning`, boolean: Off by default: the device only opens its setup AP on first run. Turning this on lets it reopen that AP any time WiFi drops, not just once -- only do this on a trusted, physically-controlled network. Anyone in radio range while WiFi is down could otherwise connect to the AP and redirect this device to a different network.

Defaults: `{"credentialName":"","security":"password","allowReprovisioning":false}`
